- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to undercorrect — force upward adjustment in forecast mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and continues upward trend — cap growth rate at 2–3% per day post-spike.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d), model underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model fails to anticipate reversal — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When bullish sentiment is low but supply net is negative, model often ignores policy impact — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast mean.
- In multi-day auction periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive CAP3 EU auctions), model tends to overestimate price stability — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 50% of 30d mean), model fails to recognize — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model often overestimates volatility — reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 5 days.
